name: Snapseed

changelog: Broader RAW support, including DNG, ARW, RAF, NEF, CR3, ORF and PEF files.
Undo and redo for most actions inside editing tools.
Many more improvements and bug fixes.

summary: Snapseed is Google's free photo editor for Android, with professional tools like curves, selective adjustments, healing and RAW editing. The latest Snapseed APK is version 4.1, updated October 23, 2026, which adds support for many more RAW formats and undo and redo. It's completely free, with no ads and no in-app purchases.
metaDescription: Get the official Snapseed APK 4.1 for Android: Google's free photo editor with RAW support, curves and healing. What's new, tips, install steps and FAQ.

faq.q: How do I install Snapseed on Android?
faq.a: Open Google Play, search for Snapseed and check the developer is Google LLC before tapping Install. Google Play only shows the Install button if your phone is compatible. It's free to install, and Play keeps it updated automatically, so you never need to download an APK by hand. Avoid copies from other sites: they aren't from Google LLC and may be altered, so the safest way to use Snapseed is the official listing.

Yes, completely. Snapseed is made by Google and is free to download and use, with no ads, no subscriptions and no in-app purchases. Every tool is available to everyone, which is rare for a photo editor this capable.

Yes. Snapseed 4.1 expanded RAW support to many more formats, including DNG and the RAW files from Sony (ARW), Fujifilm (RAF), Nikon (NEF), Canon (CR3), Olympus (ORF) and Pentax (PEF) cameras. Open the file as usual and Snapseed's tools work on the full RAW data.

No. Snapseed never adds a watermark to your photos. When you export, you get your edited image at full quality with nothing added, whether you save a copy, export to a folder or share directly to another app.

faq.q: Can I undo edits in Snapseed?
faq.a: Yes. Version 4.1 added undo and redo for most actions inside tools. Snapseed has also always kept your edits as a stack you can revisit: tap the edit history to remove or change an earlier step without starting again.
